Generate and Compile a C++ ODE Solver

Source: R/cppODE.R
cppODE.Rd

Generates C++ source code for an ODE system \(\dot{x} = f(x, p)\), compiles it via R CMD SHLIB, and returns a handle for use with solveODE(). The four available methods ("bdf", "adams", "rb4", "tsit5") and their selection criteria, the dual-number sensitivity framework, and the event handling are described in the articles Stepping and error control, Forward sensitivities and Events, switches and saltation.

Usage

cppODE(
  rhs,
  events = NULL,
  rootfunc = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  forcings = NULL,
  compile = TRUE,
  modelname = NULL,
  outdir = tempdir(),
  deriv = TRUE,
  deriv2 = FALSE,
  includeTimeZero = TRUE,
  useDenseOutput = TRUE,
  sparse = NULL,
  method = c("bdf", "adams", "rb4", "tsit5"),
  useNDF = TRUE,
  derivMode = c("forward", "reverse", "forward-forward", "forward-reverse"),
  profile = FALSE,
  stepTrace = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

rhs

Named character vector of ODE right-hand sides, see expressions. Names are the state variables.

events

Optional event data.frame, see Details. Default NULL.

rootfunc

Optional integration-termination root: "equilibrate" or a character vector of expressions. Default NULL.

fixed

Optional character vector of state or parameter names excluded from sensitivities at compile time. Default NULL.

forcings

Optional character vector, the names of the forcings in rhs. Their data go to forcings of solveODE(). Default NULL.

compile

Logical. Compile and load the generated C++ code. Default TRUE; with FALSE, compile several models together with compile().

modelname

Optional base name for the generated source file and exported C symbols. A random identifier is used when NULL.

outdir

Directory for the generated C++ source. Default tempdir().

deriv

Logical. Compute first-order parameter sensitivities. Default TRUE. Ignored under derivMode = "reverse" and "forward-reverse".

deriv2

Logical. Compute second-order parameter sensitivities; implies deriv = TRUE. Default FALSE. derivMode = "forward-forward" is the preferred spelling.

includeTimeZero

Logical. Ensure that 0 is part of the integration times. Default TRUE.

useDenseOutput

Logical. Use the dense output of the method for user-requested time points. Default TRUE. Applies to method = "rb4" and "tsit5", whose interpolant is of lower order than the method; FALSE makes the solver land on each requested time exactly. FALSE is ignored with a warning for "bdf" and "adams" and under the reverse modes.

sparse

Logical or NULL. NULL (default) selects sparse or dense LU from the Jacobian sparsity; TRUE forces sparse, FALSE forces dense. Sparse LU requires KLU at install time, see installLibs().

method

Integration method: "bdf" (default), "adams", "rb4", or "tsit5".

useNDF

Logical. Use the NDF coefficients of Shampine and Reichelt in the BDF corrector. Default TRUE. Applies to method = "bdf"; ignored otherwise.

derivMode

Direction the derivatives are taken in.

  • "forward" (default): forward sensitivities as built by deriv, returned as $tangent.

  • "reverse": no forward sensitivities; the model takes a cotangent in solveODE() and returns $cotangent, one row per state and parameter. Under "bdf" the sweep solves the corrector equation of every step to reltol and abstol, under "adams" it transposes the corrector iterations the value run took.

  • "forward-forward": the same as deriv2 = TRUE, returning $hessian.

  • "forward-reverse": returns $tangent, $cotangent and $curvature, the derivatives of $cotangent along each tangent direction, with the corrector treated as under "reverse".

profile

Logical, default FALSE. Compile with timers that print a summary per category to the standard error stream after each solve.

stepTrace

Logical, default FALSE. Compile to record per-step diagnostics, returned as $trace by solveODE().

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages. Default FALSE.

Value

The compiled model name (character) with the attributes required by solveODE(): equations, srcfile, variables, parameters, forcings, events, rootfunc, fixed (the compile-time set), deriv, deriv2, derivMode, sparse, method ("rosenbrock4" for "rb4"), useNDF, solveAbi, dimNames (with element sens only when deriv is TRUE), compileArgs, and linkArgs when OpenMP is available.

Details

Events are specified as a data.frame with columns var (affected variable), value (expression to apply), method ("replace", "add", or "multiply"), and exactly one of time (event time) or root (root expression); any other column is an error. A root event fires on crossings in both directions. rootfunc terminates integration: "equilibrate" stops at steady state (see roottol in solveODE()); a character vector of expressions stops at the first zero crossing.

A time event fires when the event time lies between the first and the last integration time, the first included and the last not; with includeTimeZero the integration times contain 0. An event at the first time is applied before the solve starts, and one inside the window adds the event time to the output, with the state after the event in that row. An event before the first or at or after the last time is ignored and changes neither the output nor the span of the integration. A grid of a single time applies the events at that time.

A comparison <, <=, >, >= whose sides differ by an amount that reads a state or the time, inside piecewise(), a logical operator or a product, and Heaviside() or sign() of such an amount, switch the right-hand side where the amount crosses zero, for instance "piecewise(1, time > ts && time <= t2, 0)" or "kin - v*(x > 0)". The solver locates each crossing as a root, so a short pulse is not stepped over, and the sensitivities take the jump. A switch adds no output row and is not limited by maxroot. Each branch is evaluated a step beyond the switch, so it has to be defined there. Where both branches push the solution onto the switching surface, it slides along it. Events, switches and saltation describes how crossings and slides are solved. == and != are evaluated as written.

See also

expressions for the syntax of equations; solveODE() for integration; cvode() for the SUNDIALS-backed alternative; cppFUN() for algebraic functions; Code generation, Stepping and error control, Forward sensitivities, Events, switches and saltation Reverse mode: the discrete adjoint and Events in reverse mode on the cppDE site.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (codegenAvailable()) {
  ## Six variants of one decay chain A -> B. Each is generated first and all
  ## are compiled together afterwards, into one shared object in tempdir().
  eqns <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")

  ## First-order sensitivities, the default
  fwd <- cppODE(eqns, compile = FALSE)

  ## A dose of A at the parameter time t_e
  events <- data.frame(var = "A", time = "t_e", value = 1, method = "add")
  dosed  <- cppODE(eqns, events = events, compile = FALSE)

  ## A constant inflow k0, integrated until the steady state
  steady <- cppODE(c(A = "k0 - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B"),
                   rootfunc = "equilibrate", compile = FALSE)

  ## A time-dependent input u, given as data when solving
  forced <- cppODE(c(A = "u - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B"), forcings = "u",
                   compile = FALSE)

  ## Second-order sensitivities
  fwd2 <- cppODE(eqns, deriv2 = TRUE, compile = FALSE)

  ## Reverse mode: the states in plain double, the derivatives from one
  ## backward sweep whose cost does not grow with the number of parameters
  rev <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", compile = FALSE)

  compile(fwd, dosed, steady, forced, fwd2, rev, output = "cppODE_examples")

  times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.5)
  parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)

  out <- solveODE(fwd, times, parms)
  head(out$variable)
  out$tangent[21, "B", ]                # dB(10) / d(A, B, k1, k2)

  out <- solveODE(dosed, times, c(parms, t_e = 4))
  out$variable[times %in% c(3.5, 4, 4.5), ]

  out <- solveODE(steady, times = c(0, 1000), c(parms, k0 = 1))
  tail(out$time, 1)                     # stopped before t = 1000
  tail(out$variable, 1)                 # the steady state

  u   <- list(u = data.frame(time = times, value = 1 + sin(times)))
  out <- solveODE(forced, times, parms, forcings = u)
  out$variable[21, ]

  out <- solveODE(fwd2, times, parms)
  out$hessian[21, "B", , ]              # Hessian of B(10)

  ## The gradient of sum(B) over the grid: a cotangent of ones on B
  onB <- cbind(A = 0, B = rep(1, length(times)))
  solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = onB)$cotangent
}
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC -fopenmp]
#>          [,1]
#> A    7.873989
#> B    9.221522
#> k1   2.280325
#> k2 -24.301792
# }
